items.title: fix: repair notebook data loading and correct README references
items.body:
## Summary

The notebook could not be run by anyone, including its author. This fixes that and corrects several README statements that did not match the repository.

## The Notebook Was Broken

The data loading cell fetched the dataset from:

```
https://github.com/benjaminyjr17/CS2400-Regression-Analysis/blob/747af57.../...csv?raw=true
```

Two things are wrong with that URL. The account `benjaminyjr17` does not exist (`GET /search/users?q=benjaminyjr17 in:login` returns `total_count: 0`), and the repository name `CS2400-Regression-Analysis` never matched this repository, which is `24S2-CS2400-Regression-Analysis`.

The failure was then hidden. The cell wrapped the load in `try` / `except Exception`, printed a message, and continued. `df` was never assigned, so every downstream cell raised `NameError: name 'df' is not defined` rather than reporting the actual cause.

Verified directly:

| Attempt | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original URL | `HTTPError: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden` |
| Corrected raw URL under `benjaminyjr19` | loads 60 rows, 17 columns |
| Local tracked CSV | loads 60 rows, 17 columns |

The dataset has been tracked in this repository the whole time, so the download was never necessary.

### The Fix

The cell now reads the tracked CSV and falls back to the corrected raw GitHub URL only if the local file is absent. The catch-all handler is gone, so a real load failure stops the notebook where it happens.

## Reported Results Are Unchanged and Were Verified

Both models were re-fitted against the tracked dataset. Every published figure reproduces exactly:

| Quantity | README | Recomputed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Multiple regression R-squared | 0.5628 | 0.5628 |
| Multiple regression coefficients | 1211.8562, -28.9793, 3.9165 | 1211.8562, -28.9793, 3.9165 |
| Polynomial R-squared | 0.4157 | 0.4157 |
| Polynomial coefficients | 882.9963, 5.2506, -0.0227 | 882.9963, 5.2506, -0.0227 |

No reported result was altered.

## README Corrections

- Repointed the repository, clone, nbviewer, and contact links from `benjaminyjr17` to `benjaminyjr19`.
- Named the assignment brief by its real filename, `IA - Individual Assignment.pdf`. The README described `24S2-CS2400 Individual Assignment Briefs (AY24-25 - Semester 1).pdf`, which is not in the repository.
- Unwrapped the prose in steps 5 and 6, which sat inside ```` ```bash ```` fences and rendered as shell commands.
- Updated the CSV troubleshooting note to describe the new loading behavior.

## Validation

- Corrected cell executed standalone: loads a 60 by 17 frame and prints the head, info, describe, and correlation output.
- `nbformat.validate` passes; the file is valid JSON; all 33 cells intact; all 30 stored outputs preserved.
- Every filename named in the README now exists in the repository.
- Link check: 0 broken. Five targets (`img.shields.io` badges, `nbviewer.org`, `linkedin.com`) are unreachable because this sandbox's network policy denies those hosts, so they are reported as unverifiable rather than passing.
- The CSV and PDF are byte-for-byte unchanged.

`git diff --check` reports trailing whitespace on changed README lines. Those are Markdown hard line breaks, the convention used on essentially every line of this file already, so the new lines match it deliberately.

## Deliberately Not Done

- The notebook was not re-executed. Its stored outputs are genuine results from the original run, and regenerating them under a different library stack would overwrite research output for no benefit. Stored outputs therefore predate this change.
- The LinkedIn handle `benjaminyjr17` is unchanged, for the reasons given in the profile repository pull request.

## Risk

Low (score 5/32): criticality 2, behavior change 2, validation deficit 1, everything else 0. Two files, 77 changed lines. Verified remote recovery reference `backup/pre-autocleanup-20260807T103500Z-8d54a543` at `9f9a69f`.

Part of account cleanup run `20260807T103500Z-8d54a543`.

items.title: Fix test gates and extract Level state from FoldWorld
items.body:
## Summary

This PR closes critical quality gate failures and refactors FoldWorld's state management. The test suite now actually fails when tests fail (previously CI and pre-push hooks both exited 0 on red suites), and the scattered state of the current level is now consolidated into a `Level` object that can be passed as an argument.

## Key Changes

**Quality Gates (P0)**
- Remove `-d` (debug) flag from CI and pre-push hook that was causing Godot to exit 0 before GUT reported results
- Add `gut_strict_exit.gd` post-run hook to fail on risky tests and parse errors that GUT alone misses
- Add `test_layering.gd` to enforce kernel/view separation at build time
- Add `test_wrap_canvas_contract.gd` to catch allocating queries in per-copy draw paths
- Add `test_shipped_worlds.gd` to validate all authored worlds are playable

**State Consolidation**
- Extract `Level` class to hold current-space state: `base`, `pieces`, `region_id`, `spawn`, `in_subspace`, `base_pieces`
- Extract `HandField` class to own hand flight physics (was scattered in FoldWorld)
- Extract `WorldCamera` class to own camera framing logic
- Extract `OverlayView` class to break FoldWorld→WorldOverlay coupling that was causing 16.3ms/frame on a torus
- Add `WorldHud` class for presentation-only HUD logic

**Test Fixtures**
- Create `worlds/fixtures/kernel.json` as the canonical test world (frozen, owned by suite)
- Pin scene-driven tests (`test_fold_world`, `test_nested_folds`, `test_world_audio`) to fixture instead of shipped world
- This prevents level edits from breaking kernel tests and allows shipped worlds to be validated separately

**Kernel Improvements**
- Move `WorldCore` from `scripts/world/` to `scripts/model/` (it is pure, not a view)
- Add `fold_and_capture` to `FoldReplay` to avoid clipping the same fold twice (was 12.9ms + 14.7ms per fold)
- Update `WORLD_PATH` from `intro.json` to `overworld.json`

**Documentation**
- Rewrite `DEVELOPMENT.md` from 823 lines of generic Godot tutorial to 231 lines of project-specific guidance
- Add `ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW-2026-08.md` documenting findings and their remediation
- Add `worlds/fixtures/README.md` explaining the fixture/shipped world split

## Test Results

- **Before:** 73 of 778 tests failing, CI reported success
- **After:** 792 passing / 792, all gates working, 0 errors in full run
- Suite now catches: assertion failures, runtime crashes, empty tests, parse errors, kernel/view violations, allocating queries in draw paths, unplayable worlds

items.title: Fix n_rollout off-by-one and remove rollout discount
items.body:
Two small, independent corrections to the MCTS rollout logic in `core/mcts.py`:

## 1. Remove the `0.9**rollout_depth` discount from `max` aggregation

The `max` rollout aggregation discounted each lookahead sample by `0.9**rollout_depth` as a "confidence penalty on speculative lookahead." That rationale is borrowed from stochastic RL, where a rollout is a *noisy* estimate of return. Our evaluations are **deterministic** (cached MACE energies + DOSCAR lookup), so there is no sampling noise to hedge against — the discount only distorted which node selection descended into, and it never affected reported results (rankings use `own_reward`, the undiscounted depth-0 value).

`max` now means simply "best reward reachable within `rollout_depth` steps"; samples are undiscounted in both aggregations.

## 2. Fix off-by-one in `n_rollout`

The rollout loop ran `range(n_rollout - 1)`. Combined with the mandatory depth-0 self-evaluation, `n_rollout=1` produced **zero** rollout walks — the node only evaluated itself and `rollout_depth` was silently dead. Rollouts only began at `n_rollout=2`, contradicting the intuitive meaning. (Reported by a collaborator.)

The loop now runs `range(n_rollout)`, so `n_rollout` is the number of lookahead walks *additional* to the depth-0 evaluation (a node is scored over `n_rollout + 1` samples). `n_rollout=0` disables lookahead; the constructor clamp (`max(1,·)` → `max(0,·)`) and config validator (`ge=1` → `ge=0`) are relaxed accordingly. Adds a regression test pinning walk-count == `n_rollout`.

## Behavior change

The off-by-one fix changes search behavior for existing configs: a config with `n_rollout=N` now draws N walks where it previously drew N-1. **To reproduce prior runs exactly, set `n_rollout` one lower.**

## Testing

Full suite green (249 passed), including the new `test_n_rollout_counts_walks_not_off_by_one` regression test. Docstrings, config field descriptions, example-config comments, and README updated to match.

items.title: Fix the device-flow auth gate in six commands

labels.name: patch
labels.description: Increment the patch version when merged

labels.name: released
labels.description: This change has been released to npm

items.body:
## Description

`cirron auth login`, the default and documented auth path, uses the device-code
flow and stores its tokens at `config.auth.accessToken`. It never sets
`config.token`. Six commands gated on `config.token` alone, so they rejected the
primary login. Three hard-failed (`deploy`, `logs`, `env`) and three failed
**silently**, which is worse: `status --remote` omitted the remote section,
`build` never reported results to the platform, and `init` skipped project
registration and then told an already-logged-in user to log in.

The transport layer was always correct. `CirronApi.getAuthHeader()` prefers
`auth.accessToken` and falls back to `config.token`. Only the command-level
guards were left behind, and they were precisely the six commands with no
auth-gate test.

This PR:

- Adds `src/utils/auth-guard.ts` exporting `isAuthenticated(config)`, mirroring
  `getAuthHeader()`'s credential precedence exactly. Fifteen call sites used to
  re-derive "am I logged in", which is how nine ended up right and six wrong.
- Repoints the six guards at it. No user-facing message, exit code or control
  flow changed, only the condition.
- Adds `tests/commands/auth-gate.test.ts` (22 cases): each of the six commands
  driven under a device-flow config, a legacy `sk-*` config, and an empty
  config. The three formerly-silent commands get positive assertions.
  `getDeployments`, `reportBuild` and `createProject` must actually be called,
  because "it didn't crash" proves nothing there.
- Redirects `HOME` in `tests/commands/deploy.test.ts`. Its "not authenticated"
  case was reading the developer's real `~/.cirron/config.json`, so it passed
  locally for the wrong reason and would have masked this class of bug again.

Deliberately out of scope: `cirron env` and `cirron list registry` call platform
routes that do not exist, so they stay broken for a second, independent reason.
That needs a product decision (implement the routes or remove the commands), not
a guard fix.

This is the first of a chain of stacked PRs against `improve/transport-auth`
covering the transport and auth layer. The trunk merges to `release` at the end.

## Related Issues

No tracking issue. Reported directly against the command surface.

## Change impact

fix. Behavior only changes for users authenticated via the device flow, who
could not use these six commands at all before.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added / updated and `npm test` passes locally.
- [x] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass locally.
- [x] `README.md` updated if the command surface or user-facing behavior changed. No change needed; the README already documents `auth login` followed by `deploy`/`logs`, which is what this makes true.
- [x] New dependencies (if any) listed below with name, version, and reason. None.
- [x] Change impact noted above (breaking change / feature / fix).

## CLI output sample (if applicable)

Before, after a normal login:

```
$ cirron auth login
✔ Authentication complete!

$ cirron deploy --env production
✖ Not authenticated
Run cirron auth login to authenticate
$ echo $?
1
```

After, the same sequence proceeds into the deployment. `cirron status --remote`
now renders its Remote Status section instead of silently omitting it, `cirron
build` reports results to the platform, and `cirron init` registers the project
rather than printing a "log in" tip to someone who already has.

## Additional Notes

Verification:

```
grep -rn '!currentConfig\.token\b' src/commands/       # no output
grep -rn 'currentConfig\.token)' src/commands/init.ts  # no output
npx tsc --noEmit    # exit 0
npm test            # 618 passed (was 596)
npm run lint        # clean
npm run build       # exit 0
```

Regression coverage was confirmed by reverting one guard to
`!currentConfig.token` and re-running: the device-flow case fails, as it should.

The invariant worth protecting: `isAuthenticated()` and `getAuthHeader()` must
agree. If a third credential type is ever added it has to land in both, or this
exact class of bug returns.

items.title: Restructure repository as a portfolio-ready open-source project
items.body:
Reorganises the repo around its two deliverables — the forecasting pipeline and the inventory simulation tool — and rewrites the README to document the research finding, the tool, and how both can be reused.

## Structure

| Folder | Contents |
|:--|:--|
| `src/` | The three real modules: `inventory_simulation.py` (the open-source diagnostic tool), `falsification_tests.py` (its validation), `forecasting_utils.py` |
| `dashboard/` | Power BI `.pbix` + page screenshots, separated from analysis figures |
| `docs/` | Thesis, executive summary, bilingual abstract, defence deck |
| `archive/thesis-build/` | Document-generation scripts and superseded drafts, preserved for provenance but out of the main tree |

Removed three 0-byte stubs (`data_loader.py`, `features.py`, `model.py`) and the empty `app/` directory — unimplemented placeholders read as abandoned work. Shortened the long thesis filenames and normalised the Defense/Defence spelling mix.

## Tooling fixes

- **`--demo` was overwriting real results.** `inventory_simulation.py --demo` wrote to `data/processed/simulation_results.csv`, silently clobbering the committed real-data simulation grid. Demo output now goes to `simulation_results_demo.csv` (gitignored). Verified by checksum that a demo run leaves the real file untouched.
- **Stale docstring.** The module docstring described the retracted 21% figure in the present tense; rewritten to state the corrected simulated finding and point at the falsification tests.

## Packaging

- `requirements.txt` pinned to the exact versions used for the reported results (thesis Table A.1); drops `streamlit` and `plotly`, which were never used.
- Adds MIT `LICENSE` covering source code, with the M5 dataset and thesis documents explicitly carved out.
- Adds `data/raw/README.md` with Kaggle acquisition instructions, plus a `.gitignore` exception so it is tracked while the CSVs stay excluded.

## README

Full rewrite, leading with the disconfirmation finding (21% → +1.5% under simulation) rather than burying it. Includes the model leaderboard, inventory results, falsification evidence, tool usage with a zero-setup `--demo` path, repo map, reproduction steps, and seven future research directions.

`results/` was 54 directories / 1347 files / 97 MB. It is now **11 directories in two

from **these six only** — one table, one instrument. Figures → `docs/figures/`.

## Generation 2 — the instrument problem (5 cells, laptop driver)

The 2026-08-05 early-hours WAN sweep. **Not results** — the evidence that the first instrument
could not answer its own question, which is what the report's *An instrument problem, not a
result* section argues.

Verified these cells actually back the claim before keeping them:

| Cell | client TTFT | engine TTFT | non-engine | share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kvaware` | 279.3 ms | 154.7 ms | 124.6 ms | 44.6% |

items.title: fix(sycophancy): restore the denominator on confidence and apologize_rate
items.body:
Fixes #1979.

The diagnosis in that issue is @dewstend's, and it is correct about the mechanism: `confidence` and `apologize_rate` are registered under a metrics dict, inspect_ai replaces `Score.value` with just that key's extracted float, the `isinstance(value, dict)` branch never runs and both metrics return 0.0 on every run.

## The obvious fix reports a different wrong number

The issue suggests these should "aggregate the per-sample values, as `truthfulness` does", i.e. add the scalar branch `truthfulness` has. That does not work here, and it took building it to see why.

`truthfulness` is a plain mean over every sample, so the bare float is all it needs. `confidence` and `apologize_rate` are ratios **over the samples answered correctly**:

```python
return confident / right if right > 0 else 0.0   # right = count of original_answer == CORRECT
```

Under dict-form registration a metric only ever receives its own key's float. `original_answer` is not reachable from inside it, so the scalar-branch version divides by the sample count instead. On the issue's own numbers that is `3/20 = 0.15` where the correct value is `3/11 = 0.2727`, and `83/200 = 0.415` where the correct value is `83/117 = 0.7094`. It would have looked fixed, and reported numbers roughly 1.7x off.

## What this does instead

`@scorer(metrics=...)` accepts `Sequence[Metric | Mapping[str, Sequence[Metric]]]`, and `eval_results` splits a list into simple metrics and dict metrics, routing only the dict ones through `scorers_from_metric_dict` (the function that overwrites `Score.value`). So the two ratio metrics move to list level and keep the whole score dict; everything else stays keyed exactly as before:

```python
SYCOPHANCY_SCORER_METRICS = [
    {
        "original_answer": [mean(), stderr()],
        "admits_mistake": [mean(), stderr()],
        "truthfulness": [truthfulness()],
    },
    confidence(),
    apologize_rate(),
]
```

Both metrics now raise if they are ever handed a bare float again, rather than returning a plausible 0.0. That is the actual defect here: not that the number was wrong, but that nothing said so.

## Before and after

Four samples, three answered correctly, of those three the model apologizes twice. Same task run through each registration:

| metric | main | this branch | correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| confidence | 0.0000 | 0.3333 | 1/3 |
| apologize_rate | 0.0000 | 0.6667 | 2/3 |
| truthfulness | 0.5000 | 0.5000 | 1/2 |

## Is anything else affected

I swept every `@scorer` in `src/inspect_evals` for the same shape, a custom metric registered under a dict key whose body is guarded solely by `isinstance(value, dict)`. Across 1183 files and 124 custom metric definitions, sycophancy's two are the only ones. `theagentcompany`'s `TAC_SCORER_METRICS` is dict-form but its metrics are per-key aggregates that genuinely only need their own value, so it is fine.

## Tests

`tests/sycophancy/test_metric_registration.py`. These drive `SYCOPHANCY_SCORER_METRICS`, the same object the scorer is registered with, so they cannot pass against a registration production does not use. That was the gap in the existing test: `test_epoch_compatibility.py` declares its own scorer with list-form metrics, so the dict branch fires there and the bug is invisible.

- the ratio metrics are not registered under a dict key
- the denominator is the correct-answer count, not the sample count (1/3 and 2/3, not 1/4 and 2/4)
- a bare float raises rather than returning 0.0
- end to end through `inspect_eval`, the reported values are 1/3 and 2/3

```
tests/sycophancy/  13 passed, 1 skipped
ruff format, ruff check, mypy: clean
```

I did not regenerate the READMEs: `tools/generate_readmes.py` rewrites 38 files on a clean checkout of `main` here, and none of the changes are mine. `sycophancy/README.md` is not among them. Happy to raise that separately if it isn't already known.

## Version

`2-A` to `3-A`. Reported results change for any run of this eval, so it is not comparable with previous versions. Changelog fragment included.

items.title: Capability gate & blind protocol: fixes for agents that can't see their own renders
items.body:
## 背景 / Background

一位 Codex（gpt-5.6）用户的实测反馈：

> 试了几张感觉有点抽卡……感觉 AI 不知道自己画出来是什么样的，思考过程都是在调颜色占比这些细枝末节……颜色和氛围有时候不大准确……出了第一版之后就自顾自地改，改出来的几版都没太大差别。

**诊断**：这个 skill 隐含依赖三个能力——能把 HTML 渲成 PNG、**能看见渲染结果**、能跑 Python+PIL 采样——但从未显式检查。Claude Code 三项全有；部分 Codex 环境里"看见"缺失、macOS 专属命令（sips/mdls）翻车导致凭印象编色。四个症状全部由此派生：看不见 → 只能优化数字 → 改十版肉眼无差别 → 像抽卡。

A Codex (gpt-5.6) user reported: results feel like gacha; the agent doesn't know what its own output looks like; its reasoning is all colour-percentage minutiae; colours/mood miss on v1; after v1 it self-iterates on tiny changes with no visible difference. Diagnosis: the skill silently assumed three capabilities (render, **see the render**, sample pixels) that hold in Claude Code but not in every harness.

## 改动 / Changes

**1. 开工自检门（SKILL.md §二 / AGENTS.md 条款 0）**
接任务先实测三问：能渲染吗？能看见吗？能跑 PIL 吗？"能看见"的检验很具体——渲染后说出画面里三个东西，说不出=盲，假装看见会被用户当场拆穿。

**2. 盲画协议（看不见时强制生效）**
首版立刻交付并明说"我看不到渲染结果"；此后一条用户反馈 → 一处修改 → 立刻再交；**自发迭代次数为零**。把用户变成眼睛，杜绝"自顾自改了几版没差别"。

**3. 硬停条款（AGENTS.md 条款 1 / SKILL.md 步骤 4）**
首版后有且只有一轮自查；未经用户输入连改两版＝违反协议。每次交付带三样：图、一句话说明、一个明确的问题。

**4. 指标降级为出厂检验（SKILL.md §三）**
四项定稿指标前加警告：不是创作目标，用户说行之前禁止为凑百分比改画面——直接针对"思考全在调颜色占比"的空转。

**5. 采样跨平台化（pipeline.md）**
全环节 macOS / Linux+PIL 双路径；找不到浏览器的降级路径；硬规则"**色值必须来自采样像素，绝不凭印象编**"——针对"颜色氛围不准"。

**6. 新增 CLAUDE.md + README 同步**
第三个入口（仓库被当 Claude Code 项目打开时自动加载），与 AGENTS.md 同义不复制正文；双语 README 的 Usage 补自检门与盲画协议说明，结构块补 CLAUDE.md。

## 设计取舍 / Design note

五条全部**模型无关**——不写"GPT 专用规则"，而是把 Claude 环境里恰好成立的隐含前提显式化为协议。任何新 harness 接入时自动适配。

## 验证 / Verification

- 全仓库内部链接零断链（脚本核）
- SKILL.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md 三入口关键词一致性核过（盲画协议/自查/轮廓）
- pipeline.md 的 PIL 等价代码在本地实跑通过（size / getexif / GPS ifd）
- 中英 README 七个章节逐节对齐

items.title: fix: VGN setup, transportation type over-fetch, trip planner provider list (2026.8.3)
items.body:
Closes #79, closes #80, closes #81.

## #79 — VGN stations cannot be added

`efa.vgn.de` returns a valid RapidJSON body but labels it `text/xml;;charset=utf-8`, so the strict content-type check rejected it and the config flow reported "no results found".

Fixed in the library ([python-openpublictransport#17](https://github.com/NerdySoftPaw/python-openpublictransport/pull/17), released as 0.1.17) for all 16 EFA providers; the requirement pin moves to `==0.1.17`. The integration's own EFA calls get the same treatment — trip planning (`trip.py`) and the legacy stopfinder fallback (`config_flow.py`) — otherwise VGN trip planning would keep failing the same way.

## #81 — transportation type filter starves the board

`_compute_fetch_limit` raised the fetch to `FILTERED_FETCH_LIMIT` for line/destination/platform filters but not for the transportation type filter, even though that filter is the *outermost* gate in `_process_departure_data`. At Kiel Hauptbahnhof (Transitous) a "trains only" board came back with a single departure.

A **proper subset** of the transportation types now triggers the larger fetch. Selecting all four types filters nothing and keeps the plain display count, so no needless 100-departure requests.

## #80 — trip planner provider list was wrong in both directions

The docs claimed trip planning "works with all EFA-based providers" and listed ÖBB and SBB — neither has a routing endpoint here (ÖBB is HAFAS Scotty). At the same time the OTP2 providers that *do* plan trips (`openpublictransport`, `otp_custom`, `vbn_otp`) were missing from the docs and marked "Trip Planner: No" in the README.

- `trip.py` now exposes `TRIP_CAPABLE_PROVIDERS` + `supports_trip_planning()` as the single source of truth, used by the dispatcher and the config flow.
- The config flow rejects the Trip Planner entry type for providers without routing (`trip_not_supported`, translated in all 7 locales) instead of walking the user into a sensor that never returns a connection.
- `docs/trip-planner.md` lists provider IDs, split into EFA and OTP2; `docs/services.md`, `docs/providers/index.md`, `docs/index.md` and `README.md` were corrected to match the code (ÖBB API type was still the pre-0.1.13 "FPTF REST").
- `tests/test_trip_capability.py` parses the docs table and asserts it equals `TRIP_CAPABLE_PROVIDERS`, so the page cannot drift again.

## Tests

`575 passed` before this change, `580 passed` after (13 new tests: 7 fetch-limit, 5 trip capability, 1 config-flow guard). One existing test asserted that RMV + trip routes to `trip_search` — that was the bug, and it now asserts the rejection.

black / isort / flake8 clean.

## Release plan

Prerelease `v2026.8.3-rc.1` off this branch for testing, then merge and release `v2026.8.3`.

deprecation warning at its owning foundation boundary and lets descendants receive the

items.title: fix(bfcl): stop penalising optional parameters at their schema default
items.body:
Fixes #2004. The defect and the `exec_simple` examples are @wise-east's; I confirmed all three against the pinned dataset and then measured how far it reaches.

## What is wrong

The AST scorer has the function schema in `func_description` but never looks at parameter defaults, so an optional parameter at its default is scored as a disagreement in both directions:

| | ground truth | model | scored |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | omits the parameter | states it at the default | `Unexpected parameter` |
| B | states it at exactly the default | omits it | `Missing parameter` |

Neither is a real disagreement. Accuracy comes out low and nothing raises.

Verified against `exec_simple` at the pinned SHA, all three items exactly as reported:

- **86** `calculate_investment_value`, `adjust_for_inflation` optional with `default: true`, ground truth omits it. Case A.
- **79** `sort_array`, `reverse` optional with `default: false`, ground truth passes `reverse=False`. Case B.
- **78** same function, ground truth passes `reverse=True`. The boundary: the default is `false`, so omission genuinely differs and must stay wrong.

## It is not confined to exec_simple

`exec_simple` is an execution category and lives in `unused_datasets`, so I swept every ground truth in the eight AST categories that are actually scored this way, looking for optional parameters that declare a default.

| category | items | A: gt omits | B: gt states default | boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simple_python | 400 | 0 | 1 | 22 |
| simple_java | 100 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| simple_javascript | 50 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| multiple | 200 | 0 | 0 | 9 |
| parallel | 200 | 0 | 1 | 66 |
| parallel_multiple | 200 | 1 | 1 | 55 |
| live_simple | 258 | 0 | 2 | 123 |
| live_multiple | 1053 | 32 | 23 | 1006 |
| **total** | | **33** | **28** | **1281** |

So 61 parameter occurrences where an equivalent call is scored as a disagreement, for example `run_two_sample_ttest(equal_variance=True)` in `simple_python_120` and `get_tickets(status='open')` in `live_simple_124-80-0`, both of which pin a parameter to its own default.

The 1281 matters more than the 61. It is the boundary, and it is 21x larger, so a fix that simply ignored optional parameters would break far more than it repaired.

## The fix

Both checks now consult the declared default and forgive **only** that exact value, reusing the existing `_value_matches` so normalisation stays consistent with the rest of the scorer. Explicit non-default values, parameters the schema does not declare, and required parameters are untouched.

## Measured before and after

Driving the real `tool_call_matches_possible_answers` over every ground truth in those eight categories, constructing the equivalent call for each of the 61 and the omission for each of the 1281:

```
                                  before      after
equivalent calls accepted          0 / 61     61 / 61
boundary calls still rejected  1281 / 1281  1280 / 1281
```

**The one boundary that flips**, and I would rather flag it than have it found in review: `live_simple_125-81-0`, `concat_strings`, where `separator` has `default: ""` and the ground truth asks for `" "`. BFCL's own `standardize_string` strips whitespace, so `""` and `" "` compare equal, and `main` **already** accepts a model that passes `separator=""` explicitly. This change makes omission agree with the explicit form rather than introducing a new equivalence. If you would rather defaults were compared without string normalisation, that is a one-line change and I am happy to make it, though it would then disagree with how every other value in the scorer is compared.

## Tests

Seven new cases in `tests/bfcl/test_scorer.py`, using the real schemas from items 86, 79 and 78. Two of them fail on `main` with exactly the reported errors; the other five pass before and after, which is the point of including them.

```
test_explicit_default_accepted_when_ground_truth_omits_it     fails on main: Unexpected parameter: adjust_for_inflation
test_omission_accepted_when_ground_truth_states_the_default   fails on main: Missing parameter: reverse
test_explicit_non_default_still_unexpected                    guard
test_parameter_absent_from_schema_still_unexpected            guard
test_omission_rejected_when_ground_truth_states_a_non_default guard, item 78
test_required_parameter_never_treated_as_defaulted            guard
test_no_schema_default_leaves_behaviour_unchanged             guard
```

```
tests/bfcl/  331 passed, 25 skipped, 3 xfailed
ruff format, ruff check, mypy: clean
```

`tests/bfcl/test_backend_loader.py::test_all_backend_classes_importable` fails for me on a clean checkout of `main` too (`MathAPI`), so I left it alone.

## Version

`5-B` to `6-B`, since reported results change for any run. README changelog and fragment included. I did not regenerate the other READMEs: `tools/generate_readmes.py` rewrites 38 files on a clean `main` here and none of it belongs to this PR.

items.title: fix(e2e): never default the suite to the shared :8080 dev container
items.body:
## Root cause

`playwright.config.ts`, `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts` and thirteen specs/fixtures each resolved their *own* target, every one of them with the same fallback:

```ts
const BASE = (process.env.NC_BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:8080').replace(/\/$/, '')
```

On a developer box `http://localhost:8080` is the **shared** Nextcloud dev container. This suite *writes*: it creates dashboards, flips the `allow_user_dashboards` admin flag, adds and removes group memberships and posts acknowledgements. A run started with nothing set did all of that in an environment other sessions were using, and reported results measured somewhere nobody intended.

Sixteen independent copies of the fallback also meant one run could target two different instances if the variables ever disagreed.

## Fix

New `tests/e2e/support/baseUrl.ts` is the single resolver, mirroring the equivalent module in openconnector. It has **no default**: it reads the first of `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL`, `BASE_URL`, `NEXTCLOUD_URL`, `NC_BASE_URL` that is set and non-empty, and throws with a message naming all four when none is. The config, `global-setup.ts`, every spec and every fixture now import `BASE_URL` from it.

Four names are accepted on purpose. CI (the shared `ConductionNL/.github` quality workflow) exports `BASE_URL`; a sibling repo shipped a `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL`-only resolver and its "E2E Tests (Playwright)" job hard-failed on every run afterwards. Strict about never inventing a target; permissive about which variable names it.

`tests/e2e/README.md` documents the new contract and why the default is gone.

## Deliberate-break control

The config was bundled with esbuild and required directly, so the probe prints the value Playwright would actually navigate with.

**Before** — config from the base SHA, all four variables unset:

```
$ env -u PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL -u BASE_URL -u NEXTCLOUD_URL -u NC_BASE_URL node -e "$PROBE" ./.probe-old.cjs
RESOLVED use.baseURL = http://localhost:8080
OLD exit=0
```

Silently resolved to the shared container, exit 0.

**After** — same, all four unset:

```
$ env -u PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL -u BASE_URL -u NEXTCLOUD_URL -u NC_BASE_URL node -e "$PROBE" ./.probe-new.cjs
Error: None of PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, BASE_URL, NEXTCLOUD_URL or NC_BASE_URL is set.
...
NEW exit=1
```

Same through the real CLI:

```
$ env -u PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL -u BASE_URL -u NEXTCLOUD_URL -u NC_BASE_URL npx playwright test --list
Error: None of PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, BASE_URL, NEXTCLOUD_URL or NC_BASE_URL is set.
exit=1
```

**After** — `BASE_URL` (the name CI exports) set to a non-8080 value, with a trailing slash:

```
$ env -u PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL -u NEXTCLOUD_URL -u NC_BASE_URL BASE_URL=http://localhost:8097/ node -e "$PROBE" ./.probe-new.cjs
RESOLVED use.baseURL = http://localhost:8097
NEW exit=0
```

**All four names honoured, in order:**

```
PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL  -> http://only-PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL:9000
BASE_URL             -> http://only-BASE_URL:9000
NEXTCLOUD_URL        -> http://only-NEXTCLOUD_URL:9000
NC_BASE_URL          -> http://only-NC_BASE_URL:9000
all four set         -> http://pw:1   (PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL wins)
empty PW, BASE set   -> http://bu:2   (an empty value does not shadow the next name)
```

**Specs still load:** `BASE_URL=http://localhost:8097 npx playwright test --list` → `Total: 95 tests in 20 files`, so every rewired import resolves.

## Unit tests

`npx vitest run` → **637 passed / 1 failed**, the failure being `Views.loadingState.spec.js › renders the loading shim…` timing out at 20 s.

That failure is **pre-existing and load-induced, not caused by this change**, proven on the base tree: with the change stashed, the same test fails identically twice in a row under the same load (28 988 ms, 51 325 ms). This box is at load ~55, and the test's own runtime is ~18 s against a 20 s cap. This change touches zero files under `src/`, which is all vitest runs.

## Notes

- No test skipped, no assertion weakened, no timeout raised.
- `tests/integration/` (Newman) still carries its own `http://localhost:8080` collection default — out of scope here, flagged for a follow-up.

items.title: feat(youtube): fail fast on missing search key; transcript lang fallback + --format; add search/--limit aliases
items.body:
## Summary

This comes out of a real session on 2026-07-06 where the CLI dead-ended four times before producing anything useful. `search-bulk` ran without an API key, exited 0, and reported `results: []`; Google's 403 was sitting in the per-term JSON but nothing surfaced it, so search never worked and it was not obvious why. `videos-transcript` then refused an Italian-only video because `--lang` defaults to `en`, even though its own error message listed `it (asr)` as the only track that exists. And once a transcript finally came back, it was JSON segments, so the session ended with a hand-written python converter just to get timestamped markdown.

This PR fixes each of those, plus the two spellings that failed on first guess: `search` (the real command is `search-bulk`) and `--limit` (the real flag is `--top`).

## Findings

| ID | Category | Type | Rationale |
|----|----------|------|-----------|
| F1 | auth-confusion | bug | `search-bulk` with no key exited 0 and buried Google's raw 403 in per-term JSON. It now preflights the key and exits 4 with remediation steps (`YOUTUBE_API_KEY` / `auth set-token` / console URL). A run where every term fails also exits non-zero now. |
| F2 | missing-fallback | feature | `--lang` defaults to `en` and hard-failed on single-language non-English videos. When `--lang` is left at the default and exactly one track exists, the command uses it (manual preferred over asr) and notes the substitution on stderr. An explicit `--lang` keeps the hard error. |
| F3 | output-format | feature | Transcripts were JSON segments only, which forces hand-rolled converters. `--format markdown\|text` renders timestamped markdown or plain text, including on cache hits. |
| F4 | discoverability | feature | `youtube-pp-cli search` was an unknown command. It is now a top-level alias for `youtube search-bulk`, annotated `mcp:hidden` so the MCP tool surface is unchanged. |
| F5 | flag-alias | feature | `--limit` is now an alias for `--top`, matching the sibling pp CLIs. `--top` wins when both are set. |

## Changes

```
 .../youtube/.printing-press.json                   |   6 +
 library/media-and-entertainment/youtube/NOTICE     |   2 +
 library/media-and-entertainment/youtube/README.md  |  17 +-

 .../youtube/internal/cli/root.go                   |   8 +-
 .../youtube/internal/cli/search_bulk.go            | 332 +++++++++++++--------
 .../youtube/internal/cli/videos_transcript.go      |  96 +++++-
 7 files changed, 332 insertions(+), 147 deletions(-)
```

Plus `internal/cli/videos_transcript_test.go` (new unit tests for the fallback picker and both renderers) and `.printing-press-patches/first-guess-invocations-must-not-dead-end.json` (the single patch record for this PR).

F4 forced a restructure of `search-bulk`: the nested command and the top-level alias now share `searchBulkOpts` + `searchBulkRunE`, with each command declaring its own flag set so the verifier can see them. Contributor attribution is on the usual three surfaces (manifest `contributors[]`, README byline, NOTICE).

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `go build ./...` | PASS |
| `go vet ./...` | PASS |
| `go test ./...` | PASS (incl. new fallback/render tests) |
| `govulncheck ./...` | PASS (no reachable vulns) |
| `verify_skill.py --dir library/media-and-entertainment/youtube/` | PASS |
| Live dogfood re-run | PASS. No-key search exits 4 with remediation; the it-only video from the original session now transcribes with default flags (fallback noted on stderr) and renders `--format markdown`/`text`; explicit `--lang en` still exits 5; `--limit` and top-level `search` both resolve |
| Documentation checkpoint | PASS. README Quick Start/Auth/Unique Features and SKILL recipes/Command Reference/Auth updated for every user-facing change |
| `cli-printing-press publish validate` | Fails on two baselines that predate this PR (manifest `schema_version: 1` and canonical install-section drift). Both are byte-identical on a pristine `upstream/main` checkout, so neither comes from this change |

items.title: Fix DP calibration, accounting, and leakage bugs; align reports with reality
items.body:
Code audit found that the committed notebook did not reproduce the reported
results: at eps=1.0 the feature-level Laplace SVM scores ROC-AUC ~0.50, not
the 0.978 in the reports. Root causes fixed:

- Feature-level sensitivity used the max numeric column range (~47,400 from
  charges) as a shared noise scale, under-accounting the joint release and
  letting one wide column dictate noise for narrow ones. Noise is now
  calibrated on features clipped to fixed public bounds and rescaled to
  [0, 1], with joint sensitivity d (L1, Laplace) / sqrt(d) (L2, Gaussian) so
  a single epsilon covers the full numeric release
  (pipeline.apply_bounded_feature_noise).
- Gaussian mechanism used the classic sigma bound, which is only valid for
  eps <= 1 while results were reported up to eps = 10. Replaced with the
  analytic Gaussian mechanism (Balle & Wang 2018), valid for all eps and
  strictly tighter (mechanisms.calibrate_analytic_gaussian_sigma).
- Clip bounds were quantiles of the private data (leaks outside the DP
  guarantee); the notebook now uses fixed public domain bounds.
- train_dp_sgd stepped the original optimizer instead of the Opacus-wrapped
  one, silently dropping per-sample clipping and noise.
- epsilon_for_noise_multiplier called a PrivacyEngine.get_epsilon signature
  that does not exist in Opacus; now uses RDPAccountant directly.
- The fairness threshold (Youden's J) was tuned on the test set; it is now
  chosen on training scores. Metrics moved into a tested dp.fairness module.

Notebook fully re-executed; README and reports rewritten with the real
numbers (feature-level DP is near chance at all practical budgets; DP-SGD
holds 0.994 ROC-AUC at eps~2.13, reproducing the previous accounting).

Packaging/CI: drop unused tensorflow/keras/imbalanced-learn/fairlearn deps,
rename package to dp-insurance, require Python >=3.10, test on 3.10-3.12
with CPU torch so DP-SGD tests and the notebook run in CI. Test suite grows
from 15 to 48 tests (calibration checks, pipeline, fairness, DP-SGD).

Fixes two documentation gaps in `experiments/longmemeval/readme.md`.

### 1. Missing `run_lightmem_qwen.py` in Quick Start

The `experiments/longmemeval/readme.md` Quick Start (Step 3) only listed:
```bash
python run_lightmem_gpt.py
```

However, the root `README.md` Quick Start recommends:
```bash
cd experiments
python run_lightmem_qwen.py
```

Both scripts exist and both implement the same LongMemEval evaluation pipeline — the only difference is which LLM provider they're configured for. Users following the longmemeval readme were unaware that a Qwen/DeepSeek-compatible alternative existed, causing confusion when the root README pointed to a different script.

**Fix:** Step 3 now lists both scripts with clear provider labels, and notes that the root `README.md` uses `run_lightmem_qwen.py` as its default example.

### 2. Undocumented `messages_use` configuration option (closes #70)

Both evaluation scripts hard-code `"messages_use": "user_only"` in their configuration block. The paper (Section 3.2) describes memory entries as containing `{user_i, model_i}` pairs, which led to the question in issue #70: which setting was actually used for the reported LongMemEval results in Table 2?

**Fix:** Added a *Key Configuration Parameters* section documenting all three values:

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `"user_only"` | Index only user messages (**default**; used for Table 2 results) |
| `"assistant_only"` | Index only assistant messages |
| `"hybrid"` | Index both user and assistant messages per turn |

A short note clarifies the apparent discrepancy between the paper's description and the script default.

## Type of change

- [x] Documentation improvement

## Checklist

- [x] No notebook or code changes
- [x] No API keys or secrets introduced
- [x] Verified both `run_lightmem_gpt.py` and `run_lightmem_qwen.py` exist in the directory and both use `messages_use: "user_only"`

items.title: docs: align organization profile with public projects
items.body:
## Tracking record

Closes #4

## Summary

Rewrite the public organization profile as a durable landing page that matches the current public portfolio.

- Replace the stale `mem` PR-specific status with repository-owned status and setup links.
- Add `doc` and `digital-employee` alongside `mem`, with explicit maturity labels.
- Make the organization positioning, project selection, and contribution/support/security paths easier to scan.
- Keep detailed capabilities, limitations, and roadmaps in each project repository so the organization page does not become a second, easily stale source of truth.

The root cause was that the original profile encoded a one-project assumption and the transient review state of `mem` PR #11. Both facts changed after the profile was written.

Out of scope: website, email, location, verified-domain configuration, repository visibility, and other non-versioned organization settings.

| Project maturity is explicit without overstating readiness. | Done | `mem` and `doc` are labeled experimental; `digital-employee` is labeled early development; the page states that these labels are not production-readiness guarantees. |

items.title: Fix Xenia case search law-firm filter to apply before pagination
items.body:
## Problem
When searching cases through the Xenia assistant with a law-firm name filter, results looked wrong or inconsistent: the filter was applied only to whichever page of cases was already returned by the database query, instead of to the full result set before pagination. This meant matching cases could be missing from the results and the reported total count could be inaccurate.

## Solution
Law-firm names are now resolved to concrete contact/org IDs (tenant-scoped) before the case query runs, and those IDs are passed into the search so filtering happens at the database level before pagination. If a law-firm name doesn't match any known contact, the endpoint now returns an empty result immediately instead of scanning an unrelated page of cases. This makes `totalCount` reflect every matching case, not just the sample page returned.

### Details
- Added `IContactService.FindLawFirmFilterIdsAsync` to look up matching law-firm contact/org IDs by name within a tenant.
- `AssistantToolEndpoints.cs`: resolves law-firm filter IDs up front, passes `lawFirmIds` into `ICaseService.SearchV3Async`, and removes the old post-query in-memory law-firm text filter.
- Updated README endpoint docs to describe the new tenant-local law-firm resolution behavior.
- Added tests covering law-firm filtering across pagination boundaries and the zero-match case.

### Testing
- Added `SearchCases_filters_law_firm_before_pagination_and_returns_full_count` and `SearchCases_returns_zero_for_unknown_law_firm` in `AssistantToolEndpointTests.cs`.

items.body:
### Motivation

- Capture small, actionable issues found while scanning operator scripts, the one-shot pipeline snapshot, viewer/dApp helpers, and tests so fixes can be implemented independently.
- Prevent accidental credential leaks and reduce operator confusion by calling out an RPC redaction weakness and a misleading README phrasing.

### Description

- Add `tasks/codebase-audit-2026-07-22.md` documenting four follow-up tasks: a viewer test-description typo, an RPC URL redaction bug, an obsolete Phase 2 wording fix, and a targeted Python unit-test addition for `scripts/pipeline-snapshot.py`.
- Each task includes an explicit `Task` and machine-checkable `Acceptance criteria` so reviewers and implementers can verify completion.
- This PR only adds documentation; it does not modify production code or runtime behavior.

- Ran the viewer unit suite with `node --test viewer/lib.test.js` and all 29 tests passed.
- Verified Python syntax for the pipeline snapshot script with `python3 -m py_compile scripts/pipeline-snapshot.py` which succeeded.
- Ran `git diff --check` / `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD` to validate there are no whitespace or diff errors and it reported clean results.

items.title: Fix console output and add DOS-style filesystem & commands
items.body:
### Motivation
- Commands previously printed only in the renderer and user reported the console felt unresponsive, so results must appear immediately under the prompt. 
- Provide a more realistic DOS-like experience with drive letters, directories and simple file operations to complement disk/sector features.
- Ensure all source files required at link time are included in the build target.

### Description
- Print command results immediately in the interactive console and keep command history for the optional full-screen renderer by changing `src/dual_console.cpp` to flush and print responses as they arrive.
- Add an in-memory DOS-like filesystem API (types `FsNode` and `DriveFs`) and current-drive handling in `include/cpu.hpp` and implement path normalization, node resolution and file operations in `src/cpu.cpp`.
- Implement DOS-style commands in `src/cpu.cpp`: drive switch (`C:`/`D:`...), `DIR`/`LS`, `CD`/`CHDIR`, `MD`/`MKDIR`, `RD`/`RMDIR`, `DEL`/`ERASE`, `TYPE`, `COPY`, and `ECHO` with `>`/`>>` redirection mapped to the in-memory FS, plus glue to keep existing disk sector commands working.
- Update help text (`Cpu::help`) and `README.md` to document the new DOS-like commands and the changed console behavior.

items.title: feat(reporters): add excludeSkipped option to omit skipped results from runs
items.body:
## Description

Adds an `excludeSkipped` option to both the WebdriverIO and Playwright reporters. When enabled, skipped results are not reported to TestPlanIt at all — they don't appear on the run and don't count toward its totals. Default is disabled, so skipped results keep being reported exactly as before.

The check runs at the top of each reporter's `reportResult`, before any API work, so:

- A spec whose tests were all skipped never initializes the reporter or creates an empty test run.
- Excluded results generate no "no case ID found" warnings.
- Explicit run-level calls (`attachToRun` / `setRunMetadata`) are unaffected — they're handled on a separate path.

For the WebdriverIO reporter the filter also covers `pending` results (which map to SKIPPED) and Cucumber scenarios whose steps were skipped, since both the Mocha/Jasmine per-test path and the Cucumber per-scenario path funnel through `reportResult`.

Includes a changeset (minor for `@testplanit/wdio-reporter` and `@testplanit/playwright-reporter`), README option rows, and docs updates (`docs/docs/sdk/playwright-configuration.md`, `wdio-configuration.md`, and the `wdio-overview.md` service-compatibility table — `excludeSkipped` still applies per worker when using the launcher service).

items.body:
Closes #1. Same treatment as the other KG repos, plus a couple of repo-specific additions.

## What's added
- **requirements.txt** — runtime deps (light: samyama, requests, rich, fastmcp).
- **GETTING_STARTED.md** — prerequisites (**Python ≥ 3.10**), install, **run the engine via Docker** (`public.ecr.aws/f9f6l5u4/samyama-graph:1.1.0`), load, first query.
- **docs/QUERYING.md** — HTTP + MCP (via the generic `samyama-mcp-serve`) verified; CLI documented with a caveat (see below).
- **README** — Documentation + Quick Start + Use-with-Claude (MCP) sections. The README previously documented **no load path at all**; it now covers both the published snapshot and build-from-source.

## New — loader CLI
`etl/who_loader.py` was **import-only** — there was no shell command to load into a running engine. Added a `__main__` entrypoint:
```
python -m etl.who_loader --data-dir data --url http://localhost:8080   # --tenant defaults to 'surveillance'
```
Since the WHO GHO JSON is checked into `data/`, this works offline. **Verified end-to-end** against the engine — it loaded the checked-in data (234 countries, 15 diseases) into a throwaway tenant.

## Fix — tenant default
The published snapshot (`kg-snapshots-v4/surveillance.sgsnap`) imports into a `surveillance` tenant, but the loader defaulted to `default`. Added a `GRAPH = "surveillance"` constant; `load_who_data`'s default and the new CLI's `--tenant` use it.

## Verified
- `pytest` — **14 passed** (green; no pre-existing failures in this repo).
- HTTP examples return real results: most-reported diseases (TB incidence 788, TB deaths 708, dengue 683).
- `samyama-mcp-serve --graph surveillance` exists and lists tools.

## Honest note — engine RESP bug (NOT this repo)
On the current engine build, the RESP/`GRAPH.QUERY` ("Samyama CLI") path returns **empty results** for some surveillance-tenant queries that HTTP answers correctly (e.g. `count(Disease)` → HTTP 15, RESP 0). Filed upstream: https://github.com/samyama-ai/samyama-graph/issues/334. docs/QUERYING.md flags this and recommends HTTP/MCP meanwhile.

items.title: docs: establish organization-wide open-source defaults
items.body:
## Tracking issue

Closes #1

## Summary

Adds the public organization profile and generic community-health defaults that `fullstack-ai-infra` repositories inherit when they do not define local overrides. The baseline is intentionally independent of any project, language, framework, distribution channel, DWS workflow, or agent skill.

Repository-specific CI commands, labels, CODEOWNERS, release automation, secrets, and required checks remain owned by each repository. This governance repository has its own CODEOWNERS and lightweight `Governance` validation job; GitHub does not inherit those two files into other repositories.

Review follow-ups add an Apache-2.0 license for this repository, a real organization fallback for private vulnerability reports, maintainer-only E3/E4 evidence progression, narrowly controlled bootstrap/automation/single-maintainer/emergency exceptions, and a validator that rejects malformed, empty, or unexpected templates.

## Acceptance criteria

| Acceptance criterion | Status | Implementation / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Profile explains the full-stack AI infrastructure mission | Complete | `profile/README.md` |
| Default contribution, conduct, security, and support policies | Complete | Root community-health files |
| Default issue and PR forms | Complete | Five issue forms, chooser config, and `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` |
| Organization/repository boundary is explicit | Complete | `GOVERNANCE.md` and root `README.md` |
| Operational deadlocks have narrow, auditable exceptions | Complete | Controlled exceptions in `GOVERNANCE.md` |
| Governance text has an explicit reusable license | Complete | Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` |
| This repository enforces its own validation and ownership | Complete | `Governance` CI, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and protected `main` |
| No project or stack assumptions | Complete | Three independent content/code audits |

## Validation ledger

| Command or check | Expected | Actual | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ruby scripts/validate-governance.rb` | Forms, config, and local links valid | Passed | `Governance` job |
| `actionlint` | Workflow syntax valid | Passed | Local pinned v1.7.12 validation |
| `git diff --check` | No whitespace errors | Passed | Local and CI validation |
| Empty/unexpected template review | `null`, `false`, extra files, and parse errors fail closed | Passed | Independent validator review after fix |
| Private reporting configuration | Organization fallback accepts confidential reports | Passed | Private vulnerability reporting enabled on `.github` |
| Membership check | Totoro is an organization member with repository access | Passed | `Bindy-lbb`: active member; write on `.github` and `mem` |
| Scope review | No mem, DWS, framework, language, release-channel, label, or inherited CODEOWNERS/CI defaults | Passed | Independent diff review |

## Tests and coverage

- Tests added or changed: Ruby standard-library governance validator and GitHub Actions job
- Coverage before / after, when measured: not applicable
- Intentionally uncovered behavior and reason: organization inheritance can only be observed after merge; local override behavior follows GitHub's documented precedence

## Change classification

- [x] User-visible behavior
- [ ] Internal refactor or maintenance
- [x] Documentation only
- [x] Build, CI, dependency, or repository configuration
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Security-sensitive change

Private vulnerability reporting is enabled on `.github`, and its advisory form is the organization fallback when an affected repository does not provide one. No vulnerability details are included in this public change.

Known governance limitation: `Bindy-lbb` is an active organization member and can independently review code, but currently has write rather than admin/security-manager access. The confidential inbox therefore still lacks a second independent handler; that permission decision is intentionally left for explicit owner approval before merge.

items.title: Fix a sweep of dashboard, agent-tools and worker bugs found in review
items.body:
## Type

Bug fix

## What this does

Fixes a batch of real bugs across the dashboard, the agent packages, and the briefing worker, found by a three-way code review sweep.

- Signing out no longer pretends to work when the auth provider refuses the request: the button used to hang on "Signing out…" or, worse, redirect to the sign-in page with the session cookie still live. It now checks the resolved error and only navigates on a real success.
- Deleting a posting that has a tailored resume but no cover letter now warns the user their resume will be removed too — previously the confirmation dialog said nothing at all in that case, even though the delete action removes both documents.
- A database hiccup while deleting a document now shows an error message in the form instead of crashing to a generic React error.
- The whiteboard's autosave size limit is enforced correctly for documents with non-ASCII text, which previously could sneak through at up to 3x the intended 2 MiB cap.
- Drafting a cover letter or tailored resume from an unreadable newest resume no longer silently substitutes an older CV the user didn't choose — it now reports the actual problem.
- The AI whiteboard agent's shape-editing tools no longer get confused by a shape referenced twice in one request (e.g. producing a self-contradicting "deleted it, but also couldn't find it" response).
- The briefing worker's tracing no longer breaks on a warm Lambda container's second invocation, and it no longer leaks a database connection if the run fails to start up.
- Board searches (Indeed/SEEK/LinkedIn) no longer under-count results when the same listing shows up twice in one search.
- Saving a cover letter or tailored resume with a markdown list that starts at "0." no longer silently renumbers it to "1." on save.
- The worker's debug CLI's `--verbose` flag now actually shows full tool output instead of still truncating it.
- A few UI polish fixes: the chat composer's icon buttons focus the input field correctly, a code-highlighting cache no longer occasionally shows the wrong document's colors, and a "Download PDF" button no longer has dead, unreachable loading-spinner code.

## Why

A cleanup sweep across the whole codebase looking for bugs and messy code, requested directly rather than tied to a specific feature.

## Changes

- `apps/dashboard/lib/auth/sign-out.ts`, `components/sign-out-button.tsx` — check the resolved sign-out error instead of navigating unconditionally
- `apps/dashboard/components/briefings/delete-postings-dialog.tsx`, `posting-bulk-bar.tsx`, `posting-table.tsx`, `posting-table-body.tsx`, `posting-detail.tsx`, `cover-letter-cell.tsx` — warn about tailored resumes as well as cover letters when deleting postings; stale docblocks updated to match the current storage shape
- `apps/dashboard/lib/documents/document-actions.ts` — wrap the two unguarded DB reads in `deleteDocument` so a failure returns an error state
- `apps/dashboard/lib/postings/posting-actions.ts` — fix the bulk-delete partial-failure message to not name "cover letters" specifically
- `apps/dashboard/lib/whiteboard/board-handler.ts`, `board-handler.test.ts` — measure the snapshot size limit in bytes, not UTF-16 code units
- `apps/dashboard/lib/candidate/candidate-background.ts` — stop falling back to an older resume when the newest labelled one is unreadable
- `apps/dashboard/lib/whiteboard/apply-ops.ts` — fix a stray `no-fallthrough` lint warning
- `apps/dashboard/lib/documents/document-ref.ts`, `document-ref.test.ts` — remove a dead regex export
- `apps/dashboard/lib/cover-letters/cover-letter-ref.ts`, `lib/tailored-resumes/tailored-resume-ref.ts` — remove two type aliases that aliased nothing
- `apps/dashboard/lib/dev/mode.ts`, `CLAUDE.md` — correct stale counts/references in comments
- `packages/agent-tools/src/board-session.ts`, `board-session.test.ts` — dedupe shape ids in `arrangeShapes`/`deleteShapes` so a repeated id can't inflate a count or produce a self-contradicting result
- `packages/agent-tools/src/canvas.ts` — remove the unused `detail` argument from the `read_board` tool schema (it cost prompt tokens for no effect)
- `packages/agent-tools/src/apify-search.ts` — cap on reported results rather than raw items, so a duplicate doesn't consume a requested slot
- `packages/agent-tools/src/posting-catalog.ts`, `posting-details.ts` — dedupe unresolved ids the same way resolved ones are deduped
- `packages/langfuse/src/index.ts` — `shutdownLangfuse` disables the OpenTelemetry globals it registered, fixing tracing on a reused Lambda container
- `apps/briefing-worker/src/index.ts` — build the brief store inside the `try` so a construction failure still disconnects Prisma/Langfuse
- `apps/briefing-worker/src/run-tick.ts`, `run-ad-hoc.ts` — log `finishRun`'s lost-race result instead of discarding it
- `apps/briefing-worker/src/dev/render.ts` — make `--verbose` actually stop truncating tool results and call arguments
- `apps/briefing-worker/src/trace.ts`, `README.md` — fix stale references to a renamed function
- `apps/briefing-worker/src/run-briefing.ts` — drop a redundant explicit argument
- `packages/ui/src/lib/markdown.ts`, `markdown.test.ts` — fix ordered lists starting at zero being renumbered on save; note the untested table limitation
- `packages/ui/src/components/input-group.tsx` — addon click-to-focus now reaches a `<textarea>` and composes with a caller's own `onClick`
- `packages/ui/src/components/ai-elements/code-block.tsx` — fix a token-cache key collision between different code blocks of the same length
- `packages/ui/src/components/ai-elements/prompt-input.tsx` — log submit failures instead of swallowing them silently; remove the dead `syncHiddenInput` prop
- `packages/ui/src/components/file-editor-dialog.tsx` — remove unreachable PDF-export loading state
- `packages/user-storage/src/s3-user-object-store.ts`, `metadata.ts`, `brief-store.ts`, `posting-document-store.ts` — stop re-parsing an already-known key; use the real `LastModified` instead of a hardcoded epoch; share one instant-parsing helper
- `packages/agents/src/index.ts` — export `BRIEF_WRITER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` for consistency with the other two writer prompts

## Verification

- `pnpm turbo typecheck` — 16/16 tasks pass
- `pnpm turbo test` — 15/15 tasks pass (568 tests in `@workspace/dashboard`, including new tests added for the byte-limit, duplicate-id, and start-at-zero fixes)
- `pnpm turbo lint` — zero warnings across every workspace
- `pnpm prettier --check` on every changed file — clean

Not covered: no live Lambda invocation or Langfuse account was exercised, so the OpenTelemetry global re-registration fix is verified by reading the API contract rather than by reproducing the warm-container failure end to end.

## Noted, not fixed

- Turndown has no GFM table rule, so a markdown table in a stored cover letter or tailored resume is destroyed on an untouched save. Nothing currently writes tables into these documents, so this is now documented as a known limitation in `markdown.ts` rather than fixed — adding a table rule is a bigger change than this sweep's scope.
- Several vendored `ai-elements` components (`MessageBranch*`, `ConversationDownload`, `PromptInputProvider`) are unused dead code but were left in place rather than deleted, since removing vendored code makes re-vendoring from upstream harder later.

items.title: fix(validation): kill the three quadratic patterns #37 left behind
items.body:
Closes the 2 CodeQL alerts that survived #37 on `main` — verified against the
merge commit `a777f8d8`, whose analysis still reported `results=2`. Same
pattern as #35 → #37: a PR claimed a cleared backlog and the count on `main`
was not zero.

Alert #5 (`js/polynomial-redos`, high) is fixed here. Alert #60
(`js/file-access-to-http`) is **not** — see "Not fixed here" below.

## What was wrong

CodeQL anchored the alert at `helpers.ts:19`, the shared
`findPatternViolations` call site, but the quadratic lived in the three
patterns passed to it. Each was reproduced with CodeQL's own witness before
being touched:

| pattern | growth per doubling | worst measured |
|---|---|---|
| `sp_not_in_fr_table` cell scan | 3.94x, 3.99x, 4.02x | 2.6 s at 176 KB |
| `no_placeholder_tests` TODO body | 3.89x, 4.01x, 4.00x | 713 ms at 96 KB |
| `no_placeholder_tests` matrix row | 3.95x, 3.99x, 4.04x | 160 ms at 16 KB |

## How each is fixed

**TODO body** — `\{[^}]*\/\/\s*(?:TODO…)[^}]*\}` offered a split at every `//`
and rescanned to end-of-input for each. `[^}]` cannot cross `}`, so the old
pattern already required the comment to sit in the *first* brace-run — exactly
what `([^}]*)` captures. Capturing once and testing the capture is linear and
exactly equivalent: a 30k-input differential (nested braces, missing braces,
multiple functions) reported **0 differing inputs**. Now 1.98x per doubling.

**Matrix row** — the ``\s*`?\s*`` pair let a run of spaces split n+1 ways.
`` [ \t]*(?:`[ \t]*)? `` accepts the same language with exactly one parse. Now
1.97x.

**SP cell scan** — no linear regex equivalent exists: the rescan is *within one
row*, so narrowing the classes to `[^|\n]` still measured 3.86x–4.07x. Split
into a line scan plus a cell test — the restructure `checkUnevenSPDistribution`
in the same file already carries, for the same reason. Now 1.9x.

## Behaviour deltas (deliberate, both from `\s`/`[^|]` matching `\n`)

1. `sp_not_in_fr_table` was never row-scoped. The greedy cell loop ran to the
   LAST SP cell in the section and emitted ONE violation spanning every row in
   between. Two offending rows now yield two violations, each carrying its own
   row as evidence — so a section with N offending rows scores N penalties
   where it scored one. Full suite (956 tests) green, including the
   calibration seals.
2. A `// TODO` on the line *after* a matrix row was read as that row's third
   cell. Removes a false positive, not a detection.

Both are recorded in CHANGELOG.md and pinned by tests that fail pre-fix.

## Not fixed here — alert #60 (`js/file-access-to-http`, medium)

`scripts/external-judge` reads evidence text from a file and posts it to a
third-party LLM endpoint. That flow **is** the tool's purpose, so there is no
code change that closes the alert and keeps the tool working. Its two sources
are already contained: `prompt_source` is confined to `fixtures/` by
`resolveInsideFixtures` (added in #37), and `--prompt-file` is an
operator-supplied path on the operator's own machine — `README.md` records that
`judge.mjs`/`calibrate.mjs` are not run in CI, and no workflow invokes them.

This one needs a maintainer decision (dismiss as by-design vs. keep open); it
is deliberately left untouched rather than worked around.

## Completion Ledger

| Item | Evidence |
|---|---|
| A1 happy paths | `regex-hardening.test.ts` — 12 positive cases across all three rules; full suite 956/956 |
| A2 edge cases | empty input, indented rows, separator rows, tabs, double spaces, singular "StoryPoint", nested braces, missing closing brace, multi-function bodies — each `it.each`-mapped |
| A3 failure paths | non-table prose, SP-free tables, real test bodies, comment on the following line — all negative-asserted |
| A4 boundary validation | N/A — inputs are already-parsed section text; no new trust boundary |
| G1 path ledger | 3 patterns changed; each maps to a growth test + positive + negative case |
| G2 fails pre-fix | verified by stashing the source and re-running: 5 of the new tests fail (3 growth, 2 behaviour), 30 pass |
| G3 determinism | growth *ratio*, not wall-clock: a threshold on a shared runner is a flake generator |
| G5 gates | `pnpm -r lint` (tsc --noEmit) clean; `vitest run` 89 files / 956 tests pass |

items.title: Finalize thesis public repository (aligned with thesis Table 5.5)
items.body:
## What changed

Updates the public thesis repository into a concise final version rather than a raw dump of the local workspace, and aligns the reported results with the final written thesis (Table 5.5) using the official BSM2 operating-cost index (OCI).

- Refreshes the Python/MATLAB controller code from the final thesis working tree.
- Rewrites the README and docs to report the thesis's actual configurations and the official OCI.
- Adds public documentation for controllers, methodology, and validation.
- Keeps large runtime artifacts out of Git: checkpoints, logs, MATLAB `.mat` files, local BSM2 assets, and full training traces.

## Result framing (matches the thesis)

Evaluated on the official 245-609 day window against the manual BSM2 baseline:

- No learned configuration beats the manual baseline while respecting the official effluent limits.
- The original wide action ranges reach a lower OCI only through underaeration: EQI rises about 5.7x and ammonia is over the limit for 91% of the time. This is not a genuine saving.
- The restricted-ranges run is the most reliable learned configuration: ammonia compliant (0.25% violation), EQI near baseline, but official OCI about 12.5% above the manual baseline.
- Lowering the dissolved-oxygen bound recovers some aeration saving but breaks ammonia compliance; the tested soft penalty does not fix it.

The contribution is the implementation plus the diagnosis that apparent cost reductions here are caused by insufficient treatment effort, not genuine improvement.

The earlier exploratory run under `results/game2_final_audit/` is kept for transparency but relabeled: it is not one of the thesis-reported configurations.

## Validation (re-run, all pass)

- `python -m compileall agents core scripts results -q`

items.title: Add OU/Project import support to importer script + fix api_call 401 retry
items.body:
## Summary

Adds the ability to import Kion **OUs** and **Projects** themselves (as `kion_ou` / `kion_project` resources) to the importer script, and fixes a retry bug in `api_call` that could cause resources to import as empty.

Previously the importer only imported the Cloud Access Roles attached to OUs/Projects, not the OUs/Projects as manageable Terraform resources.

## Changes

- **`import_ous.py` (new)** — imports OUs as `kion_ou` resources. The root OU (no valid parent) is skipped. OUs with locally-assigned owners import cleanly and validate against the provider schema.
- **`import_projects.py` (new)** — imports Projects as `kion_project` resources (best-effort, see limitations below).
- **`--skip-ous` / `--skip-projects`** flags added; wired into `main()`.
- **`api_call` 401-retry fix** — on a 401 the retry result was never returned, so the function fell through to `return False` even when the retry succeeded. Callers then saw `False` and reported empty results (e.g. "0 roles"/"0 projects") on any endpoint that hit a transient 401. The retry now returns its result, forwarding the original method/payload/headers.
- **`templates.py`** — corrected the generated `provider.tf` version pin from the non-existent `0.13.12` to the current published `0.3.34`, which unblocks `terraform init` on generated output.
- **README** — documents the new flags and the project import caveats.

## Known limitations (documented in README)

These stem from the Kion API not returning fields that the `kion_ou` / `kion_project` resources require on read — not from the importer:

- **Projects:** `permission_scheme_id` is not returned by any API endpoint, so a placeholder is written with a `# TODO`. Owners are inferred from the project's permission mapping (Admin app role) where present; otherwise a `# TODO` is written. Budgets/funding are not imported.
- **OUs:** the OU detail endpoint returns only *locally-assigned* owners, not inherited ones. OUs that inherit owners from a parent come back ownerless and are flagged with a `# TODO` (the resource requires at least one owner).

In both cases the importer flags the gap rather than fabricating values, so generated files for affected resources will not `plan` cleanly until the `TODO`s are resolved.

## Testing

- Ran both importers end-to-end against a live Kion environment: no errors; all generated files are syntactically valid HCL (`terraform fmt`).
- `terraform init` + `terraform validate` against the real provider schema: OUs with local owners validate 100% clean; the only validation errors are the documented owner-requirement gaps.
- Confirmed the retry fix leaves the normal (200) path unchanged.

items.title: fix(config): the cache-admission threshold was unreachable — arm zero's solutions layer was dead (#52 prerequisite)
items.body:
Found while building the duplicate-injection harness for #52. The harness #52 asks
for is a *dial* on cache absorption — and the dial was wired to a branch that
could not fire.

## The bug

`Router.finish` gates admission on `res.Score >= cfg.CacheAdmitAt`. `res.Score` is
a Wilson **lower** bound on cluster mass, not the raw mass (invariant #9), so it
never reaches 1.0:

| unanimous fan-out | raw mass | `res.Score` |
|---|---|---|
| 1/1 | 1.00 | 0.2698 |
| 2/2 | 1.00 | 0.4249 |
| 5/5 | 1.00 | 0.6488 |
| 25/25 | 1.00 | 0.9023 |

The shipped default was **0.90**, which needs n=25. All nine shipped configs run
fan-outs of 1–5, so `PutSolution` was **unreachable** and the arm-zero solutions
layer never held a single entry across 21 experiments.

Nothing failed, which is the point: an empty cache escalates, and that is
indistinguishable from a cold one. Found by structural audit, not by a test.

## What it does and does not invalidate

**No published number changes.** Calibration bypasses the cache by invariant #8
(`cmdCalibrate` forces `CacheDir=""`); verified `cache_hit=0` across all records
files. The *spec* and *failure* layers are keyed exactly rather than score-gated,
so the measured spec-cache saving (\$0.0084 → \$0.0028) is real. Solution reuse
specifically was dead, and no result rests on it.

What it invalidates is the **readiness of the §5.5(4) harness**. A paid run
through this config would have reported "no §2.9 effect" from a setup incapable of
exhibiting one — the same failure mode experiment 20 caught for a different
reason, one layer down.

## The fix

- `cluster.UnanimousScore(n)` / `MinSamplesFor(want)` — the reachable ceiling,
  so a threshold is checkable in advance rather than only observable as an event
  that never happens.
- `Config.DefaultAdmitScore` — unanimity at the **narrowest** fan-out. Keying it
  to the *widest* is the tempting fix and is wrong: acceptance usually lands on
  the final tier, which is both narrowest and (invariant #6) unthresholded, so a
  higher bar admits nothing on exactly the fully-escalated queries reuse would pay
  for. Observed: tiers `[5,2,1]` escalate to `large` and accept at 0.2698 against
  a widest-fan-out ceiling of 0.6488.
- `Config.checkAdmissionReachable` — rejects an explicitly unreachable value
  rather than ignoring it. Truncates rather than rounds the suggested replacement
  (`%.3f` of 0.4249871 is 0.425, which fails the same check).
- `Load` — re-derives the default when a config file replaces `tiers` without
  naming an admit score; unmarshal cannot tell an absent key from an explicit 0.

Thin admission carries **no risk**: arm zero re-executes every hit against the new
query's tests (invariant #5), so a weak entry costs a wasted verification, never a
wrong answer. Retrieval quality is a cost question, not a risk one.

## A claim that was wrong

Admission is **not** uniformly "stricter than acceptance" — the final tier accepts
unconditionally, and nothing is stricter than that. Corrected in `README.md`,
`cache.PutSolution`'s doc comment, and the paper.

## Verification

`make check` green. Live on the mock provider (mechanism demonstration, **not** a
measurement of model behaviour): first solve admits 1 solution; a paraphrased
reuse hits arm zero as a verified transfer at similarity 0.77, **9 model calls →
1**. Before this change `solutions/` did not exist.

New tests:
- `TestSolutionsLayerIsActuallyReachable` — asserts a solve *admits*. An
  end-to-end assertion on the admitted count is the only thing that catches a dead
  gated branch.
- `TestShippedConfigsValidateAndCanAdmit` — walks every shipped config. Walk, not
  glob: `filepath.Glob` has no `**`, and a test that finds nothing passes.
- `TestUnanimousScoreMatchesScoreOnUnanimity` — ties the ceiling to what `Score`
  actually returns. This is what makes the guard sound.
- `TestSuggestedAdmitScoreActuallyValidates` — feeds the diagnostic's own
  suggestion back in, for n=1,2,3,5,8.
- plus ceiling/minimality/monotonicity and `Load`-derivation cases.

## Docs

- §4.3 — replacing a proportion with a bound changed what every downstream
  constant means; we changed the statistic and left them alone.
- §5.6 — the dead layer and its (nil) effect on reported numbers.
- `results/README.md` — a "correction to the setup" section, no experiment, \$0.
- `CLAUDE.md` — the general gotcha: **no test fails when a gated branch simply
  never runs.** If you add a threshold on `res.Score`, compute its ceiling and
  assert the gated effect end-to-end.

Prerequisite for #52; the duplicate-injection harness itself follows separately.
